title: Services and Service Discovery
description: Learn how Kubernetes Services provide stable networking for dynamic Pods and enable reliable communication inside and outside the cluster.

data.text: Kubernetes Pods are ephemeral. They get new IP addresses every time they restart, and they can scale up or down at any time. Hardcoding Pod IPs is impossible in production. A **Service** solves this by providing a stable network endpoint — a single DNS name and virtual IP — that never changes, even as the Pods behind it come and go.

Services work by continuously watching the Kubernetes API for Pods with matching labels. When a Pod starts or stops, the Service's internal load balancer updates automatically. Other services in the cluster talk to the Service, not directly to Pods.

terms.definition: An abstraction that defines a logical set of Pods and a policy to access them.
The default Service type; exposes the Service on an internal IP reachable only from within the cluster.
Exposes the Service on each Node's IP at a static port.
Provisions an external load balancer (in supported cloud environments) to route traffic to the Service.
A scalable way to track the IP addresses of Pods backing a Service.

data.text: Kubernetes supports four primary Service types. Choosing the right one depends on where your traffic originates and whether you need external access.

rows: Default; inter-service communication within the cluster
Direct external access without a load balancer
Production external traffic in cloud environments
Mapping a Service to an external DNS name

data.text: The most common way to create a Service is by applying a YAML manifest. The Service uses a label selector to find Pods that belong to it. Any Pod with matching labels becomes part of the Service's endpoint pool.

data.title: ClusterIP Service for internal API access
data.content: Expose a set of API Pods internally with a stable DNS name.
data.code:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: api-service
  labels:
    app: api
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: api
  ports:
  - name: http
    port: 80
    targetPort: 8080
    protocol: TCP

data.text: Once this Service is running, any Pod in the same namespace can reach your API at the DNS name `api-service` on port 80. If you need to reach it from another namespace, use the fully qualified domain name: `api-service.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local`.

A **headless Service** (ClusterIP set to `None`) does not allocate a virtual IP. Instead, DNS returns the individual Pod IPs directly. This is useful for StatefulSets where clients need to connect to specific replicas, such as peer-to-peer database clusters or distributed caches.

data.title: Headless Service for StatefulSet peer discovery
data.content: Enable direct Pod DNS resolution for a StatefulSet.
data.code:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: cassandra
spec:
  clusterIP: None
  selector:
    app: cassandra
  ports:
  - port: 9042
    name: cql

data.title: Services do not load-balance like cloud LBs
data.text: ClusterIP Services use kube-proxy rules (iptables or IPVS) for round-robin or random selection at the TCP level. They do not offer health-check-aware load balancing. For advanced traffic management, combine with an Ingress controller.

data.title: Expose applications with Services
data.description: Create and verify Service connectivity for internal and external access.
steps: Deploy two Pods with labels app=frontend and app=backend.
Create a ClusterIP Service for the backend Pods.
From a debug Pod, curl the backend Service by its DNS name.
Create a NodePort Service for the frontend and access it via node IP.
Describe the Service endpoints to see which Pod IPs are included.
data.expectedOutcome: You can reach applications through stable Service endpoints regardless of Pod IP changes.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Services provide stable network endpoints for dynamic Pods using label selectors.
ClusterIP is for internal traffic; NodePort and LoadBalancer expose services externally.
DNS names like <service>.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local let Pods discover each other.
Headless Services (clusterIP: None) return individual Pod IPs for StatefulSet use cases.
EndpointSlices track the Pod IPs backing a Service as Pods scale and move.
data.takeaway: Services are the backbone of Kubernetes networking — they make ephemeral Pods addressable and discoverable.
